chunks: From him, from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Marwān ibn Muslim, from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Faḍl, who said:

I saw Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام perform wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer), then he wiped his face with the lower part of his shirt. Then he said: “O Ismāʿīl, do like this, for indeed this is how I do.”

key_terms.بِأَسْفَلِ: With the lower part of something.
key_terms.لِلصَّلَاةِ: For salat (prayer), indicating the devotional context of the act.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام do after wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith reports an observed practice of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام after performing wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer). He wiped his face with the lower part of his shirt and instructed Ismāʿīl to do likewise, indicating an aspect of practical etiquette connected to ritual purity.
